mostWorthwhile.text: Filtering and then recovering useful substances was the most worthwhile part: it showed why the kidney doesn't just remove waste in one step.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the ureters and bladder was clear but a little repetitive, since both were named slots.

surprise.text: The filter let glucose and water through along with wastes, so useful substances had to be taken back.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary. Using the recovered fluid with the assembled kidneys was a reasonable guess to follow it to the bladder.

continue.text: I would probably continue: following a familiar organ through filtering, recovery and drainage made its job more understandable, and I'd be curious to see another system connected.
